# `.claude/settings.json`

<!-- generated by .claude/hooks/code_docs.py from .claude/settings.json (sha256 33f4169b9c7b25e381e2f38043ecf3d6ef257e1003297c4e25dd14d4a35f4231) on 2026-10-03; don't edit by hand, it's rewritten when the file changes -->

> Project-level Claude Code settings that register two asynchronous Stop hooks, one that logs decisions and one that updates the code docs, each time Claude finishes a turn.

## What it does and why

Claude Code reads `.claude/settings.json` from the project and applies it to every session started in this repo. This file contains only one setting: a `Stop` hook list. After Claude finishes answering, Claude Code runs two shell scripts in the background:

- `log-decisions.sh` extracts decisions from the conversation into `DECISIONS.md`.
- `document-code.sh` regenerates the learning docs for changed code files (this document is produced that way).

It is not a BUILD_PLAN step. It is tooling and supports the decision log and code-docs workflow. You don't run it. Claude Code loads it at session start. To check what is active, run `/hooks` inside Claude Code.

## How it fits

```
Claude finishes a turn
        |
        v
Claude Code reads .claude/settings.json -> hooks.Stop
        |
        +--> .claude/hooks/log-decisions.sh   (async)
        |        -> decision_logger.py -> DECISIONS.md
        |
        +--> .claude/hooks/document-code.sh   (async)
                 -> code_docs.py -> learning docs next to code
```

- Environment variable: `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, set by Claude Code to the absolute path of the project root.
- Scripts it calls: [log-decisions.sh](hooks/log-decisions.sh.md) and [document-code.sh](hooks/document-code.sh.md). They in turn use [decision_logger.py](hooks/decision_logger.py.md) and [code_docs.py](hooks/code_docs.py.md).

## Walkthrough

JSON has no comments, so this file is explained in blocks.

### Lines 1–3: the top-level object and the event name

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "Stop": [
```

- The file is a single JSON object. `"hooks"` is the key Claude Code looks for to find hook definitions.
- `"Stop"` is the event name. It fires when Claude finishes responding to a user message. Other events exist (for example `SessionStart`, `PreToolUse`), but only `Stop` is used here.
- The value is a list `[...]`. Each item is a *matcher group*: a set of hooks that share the same trigger condition.

### Lines 4–5: one group with a list of hooks

```json
      {
        "hooks": [
```

- This is the single group in the list. It has no `"matcher"` key, so it applies every time `Stop` fires. (`Stop` does not use matchers anyway.)
- The inner `"hooks"` list holds the commands to run. Hooks in one group are started in parallel, not one after another.

### Lines 6–10: the decision-logger hook

```json
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/log-decisions.sh",
            "async": true
          },
```

- `"type": "command"` means "run a shell command". Claude Code passes a JSON description of the session (including the transcript path) to the command on stdin.
- `"command"` is a string. In JSON, `\"` is an escaped double quote, so the shell sees `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/hooks/log-decisions.sh`.
- The quotes around `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` matter. If the project path contains a space, an unquoted variable would be split into two words. Quoting keeps it one path. Only the variable is quoted; the rest of the path has no spaces.
- Using `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` makes the command work no matter which directory Claude's shell is currently in.
- `"async": true` means Claude Code starts the script and does not wait for it. The script calls a headless Claude (which takes seconds), so without async every turn would stall. The cost is that the script's exit code can no longer block or alter Claude's behavior, and its output does not come back to Claude.
- The trailing comma on line 10 separates this hook from the next one. JSON forbids a trailing comma after the last item.

### Lines 11–15: the code-docs hook

```json
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/document-code.sh",
            "async": true
          }
```

- Same structure as the first hook, with a different script. It is also async, for the same reason.
- No comma after `}` because it is the last item in the list.
- Both scripts must be executable (`chmod +x`). Otherwise the shell reports "Permission denied" and the hook does nothing useful.

### Lines 16–20: closing brackets

```json
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

- Closes, in order: the inner hooks list, the group object, the `Stop` list, the `"hooks"` object, and the root object.

## Trace one run

1. Roman asks Claude: "Add a retry to `first_call.py`." Claude edits the file and writes its answer.
2. Claude finishes the turn, so the `Stop` event fires.
3. Claude Code finds `hooks.Stop[0].hooks`, a list of two commands.
4. `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` expands to the repo path (for example `/mnt/c/.../georgian-voice-assistant`). Both scripts are launched with the session JSON on stdin.
5. Claude Code does not wait. Roman can type the next message immediately.
6. In the background, `log-decisions.sh` checks whether the turn contained a decision and appends to `DECISIONS.md` if so. `document-code.sh` regenerates the doc for `first_call.py`.

## What can go wrong

- **Script not executable or missing:** the command fails. Because the hooks are async, you will likely not see an error in the chat. Check with `/hooks` or run the script by hand.
- **Invalid JSON** (a trailing comma, a missing quote): Claude Code can't parse the settings and ignores them or reports a settings error, so neither hook runs.
- **Hooks do not block anything.** Async means a failing script never stops Claude, and its failure is easy to miss. The scripts have to log their own problems (see their docs).
- **Recursion:** both scripts may start a headless `claude`, which would itself fire `Stop` hooks. The scripts guard against this with the `DECISION_LOGGER_CHILD` env var. This file does nothing to prevent it, so the guard must live in the scripts.
- **Trust:** hooks run arbitrary shell commands. Anyone who can edit this file in a cloned repo can run code on your machine when you open it with Claude Code.
- **Cost:** each turn can start up to two extra model calls in the background.
- **Parallel runs:** the two hooks start at the same time and both run on every turn. They don't coordinate with each other here.
